company.text: Intra-Cellular Therapies (Bedminster, NJ) develops treatments for central nervous system disorders. Its lead product, **Caplyta** (lumateperone), is a once-daily oral drug approved for schizophrenia and for bipolar I or II depression; on **Nov 6, 2025** the FDA added adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder in adults, Caplyta's fourth US indication. Pipeline asset **ITI-1284** is in Phase 2 for generalized anxiety disorder and Alzheimer's disease-related psychosis and agitation. Johnson & Johnson announced the deal in January 2025 and closed it on **April 2, 2025** (US$132 per share in cash, about US$14.6B); the stock was delisted from Nasdaq and the company now operates as a business unit within **J&J Innovative Medicine**. The old intracellulartherapies.com site now redirects to J&J Innovative Medicine.

financials.country: US — part of Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ)
financials.text: Intra-Cellular no longer reports on its own. **J&J Q3 2026** (call on Oct 13, 2026): worldwide sales **US$25.4B**, up 6% (US +9.1%). **Caplyta** passed **US$1B in year-to-date sales**, becoming J&J's 29th billion-dollar platform; US Caplyta sales grew **66.1%** in the quarter, driven by the adjunctive MDD launch, which J&J calls the fastest-growing oral branded therapy in that space.
